title: MCW Global Young Leaders Fellowship 2027 (New York and Vermont)
organization: MCW Global (Miracle Corners of the World), New York
overview: A year-long leadership fellowship for 18 to 26-year-olds from anywhere in the world who want to tackle a community issue in education, health or economic security: a one-month virtual community needs assessment, a 10-day in-person training in New York and Burlington, Vermont (20-29 July 2027), then ten months carrying out the project with an alumni mentor.
program_dates: Community Needs Assessment June-July 2027 (virtual); in-person training 20-29 July 2027 in New York and Burlington, Vermont; whole fellowship July 2027 - July 2028
deadline_text: 'Submit a completed application on or before Thursday, December 3, 2026, 11:59 PM (NYC EST time)'. Timeline: application opens 5 November 2026; first-round decisions and second-round application 21 December 2026; second round closes 8 January 2027; interviews with alumni 3-16 February 2027; acceptances 23 February 2027; confirmation 2 March 2027; U.S. visa interview date and deposit by 16 March 2027.
funding_details: Costs covered by MCW: 'International Economy Flights for international participants'; housing from the evening of 19 July to 29 July 2027 (New York University and Champlain College); three meals a day from 20 to 29 July 2027; round trip New York - Burlington; public transport to and from JFK, LaGuardia and Newark airports
Not covered: passport fees, visa fees and in-country costs (travel to the airport, extra baggage fees)
Accepted participants pay a USD 100 deposit by 16 March 2027, refunded in full in July 2027 after completing the in-person programme
Under the liability release, participants pay for any medical care during the in-person programme
The page does not use the words 'fully funded'
participation_fee: No application fee mentioned; accepted participants pay a refundable USD 100 deposit
eligibility: Aged 18 to 26 at the start of the programme (1 June 2027)
Open to young people 'from all over the world'
Demonstrate commitment to their community and identify an issue in it in education, health or economic security
Strong motivation to create positive change and interest in social projects (original ideas are valued over AI-generated responses)
Fluent in written and spoken English
Commit to the Community Needs Assessment in June, the 10-day in-person programme in July and a year carrying out the community project
Access to email and the internet throughout the year-long programme
Eligible for appropriate visa and travel documentation
nationality_requirements: Open to young people 'from all over the world'; no country list
age_requirement: 18 to 26 at the start of the programme (1 June 2027)
experience_requirement: Not stated; the essays ask for a community issue and an example of leadership
language_requirement: Fluent written and spoken English; the application, resume and recommendation letters must be in English
other_requirements: A U.S. visa: accepted participants confirm their U.S. visa interview date by 16 March 2027
Stay with the group for the whole 10-day in-person programme
Follow the graduation guidelines given on acceptance
documents_required: Online application (general information and two essays: a community issue and how you would address it; a time you used leadership skills to solve a challenge)
Two letters of recommendation, not from friends or family, with the recommender's name, position, contact details and relationship at the top
Signed liability waiver and logistics acknowledgement
application_process: Apply on applicant.mcwglobal.org by 3 December 2026, 11:59 PM New York time
21 December 2026: first-round decisions; shortlisted candidates complete a second-round application by 8 January 2027
3-16 February 2027: interviews with alumni; acceptances 23 February 2027; confirmation by 2 March 2027
By 16 March 2027: confirm the U.S. visa interview date and pay the refundable USD 100 deposit

sources.label: MCW Global: 2027 Young Leaders Fellowship - Applications are open! (eligibility, timeline, costs, liability release)

eligibility_reason: The fellowship is open worldwide and sets no degree or experience threshold, but the age limit is 26 on 1 June 2027 and the profile records only an under-30 band. Fluent English and a U.S. visa are also needed; the profile records no English level and no passport.
potential_issues: Age limit 26 on 1 June 2027: the profile's under-30 band does not show whether this is met
A U.S. visa is required and its fees are not covered; travel is withdrawn if a late visa application means the visa arrives less than a month before the programme
USD 100 deposit due by 16 March 2027, refunded after the in-person programme (NYU's USD 50 cancellation fee is deducted if a requested room is not used)
Participants pay for any medical care during the programme (liability release)
Two selection rounds and an alumni interview; essays should not be AI-generated
benefits: International economy flight to New York and back
Housing and three meals a day during the 10-day training (20-29 July 2027)
A year of mentoring by an alumni mentor while carrying out a community project
Training in vision planning and project development
relevance_reason: A travel-funded international programme with a community project, open worldwide without a degree or experience threshold. Fit depends on age (26 or younger on 1 June 2027) and on having a concrete community issue in education, health or economic security.

visa.required: Yes: a U.S. visa (the timeline asks accepted participants to confirm their U.S. visa interview date by 16 March 2027)
visa.support: Not stated; visa fees are not covered

upfront_cost_risk: Medium: refundable USD 100 deposit, passport and U.S. visa fees, travel to the airport and any medical costs
action: If you will be 26 or younger on 1 June 2027, apply by 3 December 2026 (11:59 PM New York time) with the two essays, a one-page resume and two recommendation letters; ask your recommenders now. Budget for the U.S. visa fee and the refundable USD 100 deposit.
notes: Seen in the feeds on 6-8 November 2026 (Opportunity Desk, Opportunities for Africans, Opportunities Corners). Official page read on 9 November 2026 (posted 27 October, updated 5 November 2026); MCW Global says it hosted the 29th edition of the fellowship in July 2026. The applicant portal answered HTTP 429 (too many requests) to the plain reader and was not read.

title: Hurford Youth Fellows Program 2027 (National Endowment for Democracy, Washington DC)
organization: International Forum for Democratic Studies, National Endowment for Democracy (NED), with the Hurford Foundation
overview: A four-month residential fellowship in Washington, DC (1 May - 31 August 2027) for emerging democracy leaders aged 30 or younger. Up to three fellows work on a project about a democratic challenge in their country or region and its implications for young people, produce at least one product (article, toolkit, podcast, video or similar) and join seminars with NED and its core institutes.
program_dates: 1 May - 31 August 2027 (four months in Washington, DC)
deadline_text: 'Deadlines: Applications: November 30, 2026. Recommendation Letters: December 4, 2026.' No time of day or time zone is given.
funding_details: 'Each fellow receives a monthly stipend for living expenses, basic health insurance coverage, and roundtrip economy-class travel to and from Washington, D.C., at the beginning and end of the fellowship.'
'Stipends are calculated to cover a short-term furnished rental apartment, food, local transportation, and other necessities.' The amount is not stated
Fellows who bring family members pay their dependents' travel and living costs
Visa costs are not mentioned; the page does not use the words 'fully funded'
stipend: Monthly stipend for living expenses, calculated to cover a furnished rental, food and local transport (amount not stated)
eligibility: 30 years of age or younger
Demonstrated commitment to, and experience in, advancing youth participation in democracy
Applications especially encouraged from leaders affiliated with civic organizations, human rights groups and initiatives working to strengthen democracy
A project on a democratic challenge in your country or region and its implications for young people (a study of U.S. democracy is not expected)
Open to 'emerging youth leaders from around the world'
nationality_requirements: 'Emerging youth leaders from around the world'; no country list
experience_requirement: Experience in advancing youth participation in democracy
language_requirement: Not stated; products may be created in English or another language
other_requirements: Four months' residence in Washington, DC (1 May - 31 August 2027)
Complete at least one product (article, handbook, toolkit, podcast, tech tool or video)
documents_required: Online application with a project proposal
Recommendation letters, due 4 December 2026 (number not stated on the page)
application_process: Create an account on the NED Fellowships Online Application System and choose the Hurford Youth Fellowship; submit by 30 November 2026
AI: limited use for ideas, editing and translation is acceptable; copy-pasting AI-generated answers is prohibited

sources.label: NED: Hurford Youth Fellows Program (2027 call, eligibility, financial support, deadlines)
NED Fellowships Online Application System ('intended for early-career candidates who are 30 years old or younger')

eligibility_reason: The under-30 age band fits the limit of 30 or younger, and no degree or nationality condition applies. The deciding criterion, demonstrated experience in advancing youth participation in democracy, is not recorded in the profile, whose experience is internships in logistics, public-sector research and health-campaign monitoring.
potential_issues: Up to three fellows worldwide: extremely competitive
Requires a record in youth civic or democracy work, which the profile does not show
A U.S. visa is needed (general requirement); the page does not mention visas or their cost
benefits: Four months in Washington, DC with a monthly stipend, basic health insurance and round-trip economy travel
Work with NED and its core institutes; seminars, roundtables and field trips
A published product such as an article, toolkit, podcast or video
relevance_reason: A well-funded four-month residency in Washington, but built for young democracy activists with a track record, and only three are chosen. Worth applying only with real civic or youth-participation work to show.

visa.required: Yes, for the United States (general requirement; not stated on the page)

upfront_cost_risk: Low: no fee mentioned; travel, a stipend and health insurance are provided; visa costs not stated
action: Apply by 30 November 2026 only if you have concrete experience in youth civic or democracy work and a project idea on a democratic challenge in the DRC; line up recommenders for 4 December 2026.
notes: Seen in the feeds on 7 November 2026 (Opportunities for Africans, Opportunities Corners, Opportunity Desk). The NED call page and the application system's home page were read on 9 November 2026.

title: Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme 2027 (MPhil and PhD in Mauritius)
organization: Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research, Government of the Republic of Mauritius
overview: Government of Mauritius scholarships for resident citizens of African Union member states or African Commonwealth countries to study full-time on campus at a public university in Mauritius from the 2027 intake. For a bachelor's holder the route is an MPhil (research master's) or MPhil/PhD. Applications go through the national nominating agency, which endorses at most 15 candidates per country.
city: Public universities in Mauritius (University of Mauritius, University of Technology Mauritius, Université des Mascareignes, Open University of Mauritius, Mauritius Institute of Education)
program_dates: Academic year starting in 2027 (July/September 2027 postgraduate intake). MPhil: at most two years plus six months for the thesis defence; MPhil/PhD: three years plus six months, then one year plus six months.
deadline_text: Two stages (guidelines, section 9.3): '1. Apply for a seat in a public HEI by end of January 2027. The HEI will provide the applicant a receipt of having applied for a seat.' 2. Submit the 2027 application form through the nominating agency of your country, by a deadline that agency communicates. The agency endorses at most 15 candidates and sends the files to the Ministry: 'Soft copies of all documents 17 March 2027; Hard copies of all documents 31 March 2027.' The call is dated October 2026.
funding_details: Call: 'The Scholarship will support successful candidates in meeting their tuition fees and contributing to their living expenses during their studies in Mauritius. Furthermore, the scholarship covers return airfare by the most economical route.'

Tuition and study-related fees paid up to MUR 100,000 a year for beneficiaries from SADC countries (local fees) or MUR 160,000 a year for non-SADC countries (international fees); anything above is paid by the student (1 USD = MUR 47.88 on 23 September 2026)
Monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 'as part support'; 'Students are expected to supplement this amount'
The awardee buys the ticket to Mauritius and claims a refund after arrival with the original receipts; the scholarship also covers the journey home once the studies are deemed completed

Awardees should arrive with at least USD 1,000 for the first three months; accommodation, travel and medical insurance, books and overseas fieldwork are the student's own (care in public hospitals is free)
participation_fee: No scholarship application fee stated; university application fees are not covered in the documents read
eligibility: Resident citizen of an active African Union member state or an African Commonwealth country (Mauritian nationals are not eligible)
MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD: not reached the 40th birthday by 1 January 2028 (undergraduate: over 18 and not yet 26 by 1 January 2028)

MPhil: a recognised undergraduate degree with at least an upper second class (or CPA/GPA greater than 60%) and the university's own entry requirements (University of Mauritius: a Bachelor with Honours with at least a 2nd Class in the relevant field; University of Technology, Mauritius: 2nd Class 1st Division)
Applied for a full-time on-campus programme at a public higher education institution in Mauritius for the academic year starting in 2027, with a confirmed seat at the time of final selection
Name of the proposed supervisor(s) with their written consent, and an abridged research proposal
Application endorsed by the nominating agency of the country of citizenship
Not a self-financing student already in Mauritius at the same level; no award for a level already held
nationality_requirements: Resident citizens of active African Union member states or African Commonwealth countries
The 2027 list of nominating agencies includes the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Minister of Higher Education, 6-8 Boulevard Colonel Tshatshi, Kinshasa/Gombe)
education_requirement: MPhil: undergraduate degree with at least an upper second class, or CPA/GPA greater than 60%
language_requirement: Not stated for postgraduate study in the guidelines read; each university's entry requirements apply. Certificates not in French or English need a certified translation.
other_requirements: Medical certificate completed by a registered medical practitioner (Section 6 of the form)
Passport valid for the whole course
Monthly progress reports; the allowance depends on satisfactory progress and attendance
Undertaking to leave Mauritius after the programme
documents_required: Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Application Form 2027 (Section 5 completed and endorsed by the nominating agency)
Certified copies of academic certificates and transcripts (with certified translations if not in French or English)
Receipt from the Mauritian public university for the seat application
Written consent of the proposed supervisor(s)
Abridged research proposal (title, aims, background, methodology, timeframe, equipment, supervisor)
application_process: Find a research supervisor and apply for an MPhil seat at a public university in Mauritius (for example the University of Mauritius, apply.uom.ac.mu/internationalapp) by the end of January 2027
Complete the 2027 application form and submit it with the documents to the DRC nominating agency (Ministry of Higher Education, Kinshasa/Gombe) by the date it sets
The agency endorses at most 15 candidates and sends soft copies by 17 March 2027 and hard copies by 31 March 2027 to the Ministry in Mauritius, which makes the final selection

sources.label: Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research: MASS page (2027 documents)
Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme 2027: Call for Applications (October 2026, PDF)
Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme 2027: Guidelines for Applicants (PDF)

eligibility_reason: DRC citizens are covered (the DRC has a listed nominating agency) and the age limit is met. The MPhil needs an upper-second-class degree or an average above 60%, which the profile does not record, plus a seat, a supervisor's consent and a research proposal; the national agency then endorses at most 15 candidates.
potential_issues: Partial funding only: capped tuition and an allowance that 'students are expected to supplement'
The outward ticket is refunded only after arrival, and the guidelines expect at least USD 1,000 of the student's own money for the first three months
For a bachelor's holder the only levels are MPhil or MPhil/PhD (research degrees); there is no taught master's in the scheme
Nomination goes through the DRC Ministry of Higher Education, whose internal deadline is not published on the Mauritian pages
The fee grid has separate SADC and non-SADC rates; the documents read do not say which applies to each country
Interrupting the studies to take up employment, or for any other non-medical reason, ends the scholarship and makes the awardee liable to refund the fees, allowance and airfare paid
benefits: Tuition and study-related fees up to MUR 100,000 or MUR 160,000 a year
Return airfare (outward ticket refunded after arrival)
Free care in Mauritian public hospitals
relevance_reason: A government route to a research master's in Mauritius, open to DRC citizens through a national nomination. It suits the profile's research and policy-analysis interest, but the funding is partial and the applicant must find a supervisor and write a research proposal.

visa.required: Yes: a provisional entry permit and student visa from the Passport and Immigration Office of Mauritius
visa.support: The university where the seat is secured starts the visa process

upfront_cost_risk: High: the outward ticket is paid first and refunded after arrival, and the guidelines expect at least USD 1,000 for the first three months; accommodation and insurance are the student's
action: If your Licence average is above 60% (or an upper-second equivalent), look for an MPhil supervisor at the University of Mauritius or another public university, apply for a seat before the end of January 2027, then ask the DRC Ministry of Higher Education for its MASS 2027 submission date.
